name: Surveyor 3

site.name: Oceanus Procellarum (Surveyor Crater)
site.description: Interior wall of a 200-meter crater in southeastern Oceanus Procellarum, later visited on foot by the Apollo 12 crew in November 1969.

endCause: Communications ended after sunset on May 4, 1967 as the lander entered lunar night; electronics did not reactivate after the two-week cryogenic freeze.
scientificValue: Surveyor 3 conducted the first in-situ mechanical trenching of lunar regolith alongside 6,315 television images, confirming that lunar soil possessed enough bearing strength to support crewed Apollo landings. Thirty-one months later, Apollo 12 astronauts inspected the dormant lander and returned its camera assembly to Earth to study long-term space exposure.

legacy.finding: Transmitted 6,315 high-resolution television frames mapping the inner slope of Surveyor Crater in Oceanus Procellarum.
Excavated regolith trenches up to 17.5 centimeters deep with its Soil Mechanics Surface Sampler, validating lunar surface bearing stability for Apollo Lunar Modules.
Became the only uncrewed planetary probe physically revisited by humans on another world when Apollo 12 retrieved its television camera and scoop in November 1969.
